name: Hydrogen
sources: Water and hydrocarbons. Made industrially from natural gas.
uses: Ammonia synthesis, oil refining, rocket fuel, fuel cells.
description: Lightest element. Colourless, odourless diatomic gas. Most abundant element in the universe.

name: Helium
name_origin: Greek helios: the Sun. First seen in the solar spectrum.
discoverers: Sir William Ramsay, Nils Langlet, P.T.Cleve
sources: Natural gas deposits, separated by distillation.
uses: Cryogenics, MRI magnets, balloons, diving gas mixes.
description: Inert colourless noble gas. Lowest boiling point of any element.
melting_note: at 25 atm (helium never freezes at normal pressure)
appearance: Colourless gas, exhibiting a red-orange glow when placed in a high-voltage electric field

name: Lithium
uses: Rechargeable batteries, ceramics, glass, mood-stabilising drugs.
description: Softest alkali metal and lightest metal. Reacts with air and water.

name: Beryllium
name_origin: Beryl, the mineral it was found in.
uses: Aerospace alloys, X-ray windows, telescope mirrors, electrical contacts.
description: Light, hard, grey metal. Stiff and non-magnetic. Dust is toxic.

name: Boron
discoverers: Sir H. Davy, J.L. Gay-Lussac, L.J. Thénard
uses: Borosilicate glass, detergents, fertiliser additive, ceramics, neutron absorbers.
description: Hard, dark metalloid. Forms stable oxygen compounds.
production: No world total (reported on different bases); Turkey ~1.8 Mt refined borates

name: Carbon
sources: Coal, oil, natural gas, carbonate rock, atmospheric CO2.
uses: Fuel, steelmaking, graphite, tyres, plastics, diamond tools.
description: Nonmetal that forms graphite, diamond and all organic compounds.
melting_note: sublimes near 3642 C at 1 atm; value for graphite under pressure
appearance: Black, soft (graphite) or colourless, very hard (diamond)

name: Nitrogen
sources: Air, separated by liquefaction and distillation.
uses: Fertiliser, explosives, refrigerant, food packaging, inert atmospheres.
description: Colourless, unreactive diatomic gas. 78% of the atmosphere.

name: Oxygen
sources: Air, water, silicate rock. Industrially distilled from liquid air.
uses: Steelmaking, medicine, welding, water treatment, rocket oxidiser.
description: Reactive nonmetal gas. 21% of the atmosphere. Supports combustion and respiration.

name: Fluorine
name_origin: Latin fluere: to flow (fluorspar used as a flux).
uses: Toothpaste, PTFE, refrigerants, uranium enrichment, pharmaceuticals.
description: Pale yellow gas. Most electronegative and most reactive element.

name: Neon
uses: Signs, high-voltage indicators, lasers, cryogenic coolant.
description: Inert colourless noble gas. Glows red-orange in discharge tubes.
appearance: Colourless gas exhibiting an orange-red glow when placed in a high voltage electric field

name: Sodium
name_origin: English soda. Symbol from Latin natrium.
uses: Table salt, soap, glass, street lamps, reactor coolant.
description: Soft silvery alkali metal. Reacts violently with water.

name: Magnesium
name_origin: Magnesia, a district of Thessaly, Greece.
uses: Light alloys, flares, fertiliser, antacids, refractories.
description: Light silvery alkaline-earth metal. Burns with a bright white flame.

name: Aluminum
sources: Bauxite, refined by the Bayer and Hall-Héroult processes.
uses: Packaging, aircraft, construction, power cables, cookware.
description: Light, corrosion-resistant silvery metal. Most abundant metal in the crust.

name: Silicon
uses: Chips, solar cells, glass, cement, silicones.
description: Hard, brittle metalloid and semiconductor. Second most abundant element in the crust.
production: ≈75 Mt/yr ferrosilicon + ≈75 Mt/yr silicon metal · silicon content

name: Phosphorus
uses: Fertiliser, detergents, matches, steel additives, battery materials.
description: Reactive nonmetal. Exists as white, red and black forms.
appearance: Colourless, waxy white, yellow, scarlet, red, violet, black
production: ≈240 Mt/yr · phosphate rock (USGS, via secondary source)

name: Sulfur
sources: Native deposits, oil and gas desulfurisation, sulfide ores.

name: Chlorine

description: Yellow-green toxic gas. Strong oxidiser.

name: Argon

name_origin: English potash. Symbol from Latin kalium.
